title.en: Cell, battery, lamp, switch and circuit diagrams

text.en:
Raju opened his torch and saw two cells, a bulb and a switch.
"All parts make a circuit," said his father.

An electric cell has a positive and a negative terminal and provides electric current. A battery is two or more cells connected together.
A lamp glows when current passes through its filament. A switch opens or closes the circuit: when closed, current flows; when open, it stops.
We draw circuits with symbols: a long and a short line for a cell, a circle with a cross for a lamp and a gap for an open switch.

problem.en: Why does a lamp go off when the switch is open?

text.en: An open switch breaks the circuit.

prompt.en: A friend says a lamp glows with an open switch. How will you reply?

points.en: A closed switch completes the circuit.
